Micron's advanced DRAM packaging enables the 512GB DDR5 RDIMM to unlock data center performance with speeds up to 9,200 MT/s and reduced operating power by more than 60%

BOISE, Idaho, Sept. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Micron Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: MU), today announced a major milestone in memory innovation with the successful demonstration of the world's first 512GB DDR5 module on multiple server platforms. The achievement reinforces Micron's leadership in high-performance, high-capacity server memory and provides enterprise data center and cloud customers with a path to support large and demanding AI, analytics, in-memory database and simulation-heavy workloads with greater efficiency. Leading semiconductor enablers, AMD and Intel, are both actively validating the module, which will deliver speeds up to 9,200 MT/s.

The module’s high capacity is possible due to Micron’s advanced vertical interconnect packaging innovations. This product vertically stacks DRAM dies interconnected by through-silicon vias (TSVs) to maximize density within individual DRAM packages while preserving the performance modern data center architectures demand. The module enables up to 12TB of DDR5 DRAM in a single 24-slot dual-socket server.

“Micron continues to set the pace for memory technology, delivering a new class of ultra-dense, high-performance server memory that helps customers keep larger datasets closer to the compute engines that need them,” said Raj Narasimhan, senior vice president and general manager of the Cloud Memory Business Unit at Micron. “A 512GB RDIMM enables multi-terabyte servers, supporting larger AI and database workloads, greater virtualization density and improved power efficiency, all within existing server footprints.”
Micron is collaborating closely with leading ecosystem enablers to validate the 512GB DDR5 RDIMM across next-generation server platforms, ensuring broad compatibility and a smooth path to deployment.

“AMD solutions continue to advance data center performance, scalability and efficiency as AI and data-intensive workloads reshape infrastructure requirements,” said Amit Goel, corporate vice president, Compute and Enterprise AI Platform Solutions Engineering, AMD. “Our close engineering collaboration with Micron brings compute and memory innovation together to help customers realize the full value of AMD-powered platforms. Together, we’re enabling balanced, high-performance infrastructure for the growing scale and complexity of modern workloads.”

"The growth of AI and other data-intensive workloads is placing new demands on server infrastructure, making memory capacity and bandwidth increasingly important to overall system performance," said Karin Eibschitz Segal, general manager of platform and system engineering in Intel’s Data Center Group. “Intel is working closely with Micron to validate its 512GB DDR5 RDIMM and help enable future server platforms designed to meet the growing demands of next-generation data center workloads.”
Meeting the memory demands of data-intensive workloads

The rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs), agentic AI, real-time inference and high-core-count CPU workloads is driving demand for greater server memory capacity, higher bandwidth and improved power efficiency. Micron 512GB RDIMMs address these demands by enabling larger datasets to remain resident in main memory, reducing reliance on slower storage tiers and minimizing costly data movement. The new 512GB RDIMM also improves efficiency, reducing operating power by more than 60% compared with four 128GB RDIMMs.

For memory-bound workloads such as Spark Support Vector Machines (SVM)-based data analytics, Micron 512GB RDIMMs can deliver up to 1.4 times higher performance compared to 256GB DDR5 configurations. The 512GB module also provides significant advantages for memory-intensive databases and caching platforms, including RocksDB and Redis, improving throughput, increasing concurrency and helping scale datasets more efficiently.
What the industry has to say about this future memory solution

“As data center workloads continue to grow, we are increasingly focused on how we can optimize the balance between compute, memory and efficiency across the stack," said Darrin Alves, chief information officer for Infrastructure Platforms at JPMorganChase. "Higher-capacity memory technologies like Micron’s 512GB RDIMMs will help enterprises support larger in-memory workloads, improve resource utilization and enhance the flexibility needed to scale modern computing environments."

First graduating class and fifth signing cohort highlight momentum behind Micron’s workforce development partnerships in Virginia

Micron Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: MU), one of the world’s largest semiconductor companies and the only U.S.-based manufacturer of memory, today celebrated the first graduating class of its Manassas Registered Apprenticeship Program. The company also welcomed its fifth cohort of apprentices during a signing ceremony at the company’s Manassas, Virginia site, reflecting continued momentum and demand for local pathways into semiconductor manufacturing careers. The milestone comes as Micron invests more than $2 billion to expand and modernize its Manassas fab, supporting more than 3,100 jobs.

This first graduating class in Manassas is Micron’s largest apprenticeship class to graduate across the U.S. to date, effectively doubling the program's total number of graduates nationwide. This is a proud achievement that reflects the program’s remarkable growth.

Since launching the program in April 2024 with Northern Virginia Community College (NOVA) and the National Institute for Industry and Career Advancement, Micron has hired more than 50 apprentices in Manassas, creating local opportunities to propel individuals into highly skilled careers and helping strengthen the talent pipeline needed to support the future of semiconductor manufacturing in America.

Micron’s registered apprenticeship program combines classroom learning, technical instruction and hands-on experience to create accessible pathways into advanced manufacturing careers. Designed for both recent high school graduates entering the workforce and adults seeking to transition into a new career, the program broadens access to high-demand opportunities in the semiconductor industry through an earn and learn model. NOVA provides related technical instruction, while the National Institute for Industry and Career Advancement serves as the apprenticeship program sponsor.

“We could not be more proud of today’s graduates and all they have accomplished,” said NOVA President Anne M. Kress. “Their success reflects both their hard work and the transformational strength of NOVA’s partnership with Micron. Through hands-on training, mentorship and real-world experience, these students now have the skills needed to build meaningful careers as part of a semiconductor workforce that is critical to our region and the nation. We are grateful to Micron for their continued investment in NOVA students and the workforce of the future.”

“Today’s graduates represent exactly what registered apprenticeships are designed to achieve: creating clear pathways into high-demand careers while helping employers build the skilled workforce they need to compete and grow,” said Mike Russo, president and CEO of the National Institute for Industry and Career Advancement. “Through our partnership with Micron and Northern Virginia Community College, these apprentices have combined classroom learning with hands-on experience to earn nationally recognized credentials and launch meaningful careers in semiconductor manufacturing. Their success demonstrates how industry, education and workforce partners can work together to strengthen America’s talent pipeline and support the long-term growth of the semiconductor industry.”

“Today is about more than celebrating a graduating class. It is about creating opportunity and expanding access to careers that can change lives. We are proud of our first apprenticeship graduates in Manassas and excited to welcome the next cohort as they begin their journey,” said Fran Dillard, vice president of global talent acquisition and workforce at Micron. “Building the workforce of the future starts with investing in people. Through strong partnerships, we are creating new pathways into semiconductor manufacturing, strengthening our communities and helping ensure the U.S. has the talent needed to lead for years to come. This is just the beginning.”

“This milestone is a proud moment for our Manassas team and a testament to what can be achieved when people have the opportunity to learn by doing,” said Delbert Parks, vice president and site executive of Micron Technology Virginia. “Our first graduating apprentices have built valuable technical skills while contributing to the work that powers our facility every day. As we welcome a new cohort, we are continuing to invest in the people and partnerships that help strengthen Virginia’s semiconductor workforce and support the future of advanced manufacturing in our community.”

In addition to expanding registered apprenticeship opportunities, Micron is investing $250,000 across three local Manassas-area Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs to help modernize equipment, enhance technical training and increase student access to semiconductor and advanced manufacturing career pathways. The investment is designed to strengthen awareness of high-tech career opportunities, support hands-on learning experiences and build stronger connections between secondary education, postsecondary training and employment opportunities. By partnering with local school systems and educators, Micron is developing a broader pipeline of future talent while ensuring students gain exposure to the skills needed for careers in Virginia’s growing semiconductor industry.

“Virginia is home to some of the nation’s most innovative companies and talented workers, and apprenticeship programs like this help ensure our workforce is ready to lead the future of American semiconductor manufacturing,” said U.S. Congressman Suhas Subramanyam. “Congratulations to Micron for creating pathways that combine hands-on experience, technical education and meaningful career opportunities. I look forward to celebrating all of the achievements of the first class of graduates and the newest apprentices.”

“Virginia is proud to be home to the future of American semiconductor manufacturing, which depends on high-skilled workers,” said Jessica K. Looman, Virginia secretary of labor. “Micron’s $2 billion investment in Manassas, which adds 3,100 jobs, shows what’s possible when industry and education work together to open doors for Virginians. Creating good-paying jobs and expanding economic opportunity for Virginia workers and their families remains a top priority, and I congratulate these apprentices and welcome the new cohort joining Micron’s Manassas team as they build lasting careers in one of our commonwealth’s fastest-growing industries.”

Apprentices who complete the program gain relevant technical skills and earn a U.S. Department of Labor Journeyworker Certificate, a nationally recognized credential that demonstrates mastery of their occupation and supports long-term career growth. The program creates another pathway into semiconductor manufacturing careers and helps participants build the knowledge, hands-on experience and workplace readiness to grow their careers at Micron.

Micron’s Manassas, Virginia, fab is a leading U.S. advanced semiconductor manufacturing site and the country’s only fully owned 300mm fab, producing DRAM, NAND and NOR for automotive, defense and aerospace, industrial, networking and other markets. Earlier this year, Micron began manufacturing 1α (1-alpha) DRAM at the site, the most advanced memory ever produced in the United States.

Micron is investing over $250 billion to expand its leading-edge memory manufacturing and R&D across the United States, creating over 90,000 jobs nationwide. Local talent development remains essential to the company’s long-term success and the future of the semiconductor industry. The Manassas registered apprenticeship program demonstrates Micron’s commitment to expanding access to high-tech careers, investing in local talent and strengthening semiconductor workforce readiness in Virginia and nationwide.

ASML and TSMC Announce Initiative to Pioneer Industry Transition to Large-Format Photomasks for High NA EUV
Issued by: ASML Holding N.V. and TSMC
ASML and TSMC Announce Initiative to Pioneer Industry Transition to Large-Format Photomasks for High NA EUV

On September 7, in advance of the SPIE BACUS Conference, ASML and TSMC formed a collaborative industry initiative to drive the transition to 12-inch photomasks, maximizing the value of High NA EUV lithography.
The initiative targets establishing a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031, supporting full lithography system readiness for advanced node production by 2033.
Underscoring broad industry support, High NA EUV adopters and other major suppliers, have expressed their interest to join the initiative.

ASML Holding N.V. (Euronext: ASML, Nasdaq: ASML) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TWSE: 2330, NYSE: TSM) announced a collaborative initiative to lead the semiconductor industry’s transition to a larger-format Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography photomask.

While High NA EUV will be adopted for production using the current, 6-inch masks, the transition to larger, 12-inch masks is expected to further increase fab productivity, lower chipmaking costs and remove stitching constraints, benefiting the entire semiconductor industry. It will enable advanced chip manufacturers to fully leverage the advantages of High NA EUV, making future generations of leading-edge chips more cost-effective.

“We expect the adoption of High NA EUV to increase progressively along the device scaling roadmap, first using current 6-inch masks and then further supported by 12-inch masks, which enable greater scanner productivity and allow the industry to meet the demand for smaller, faster and more energy-efficient chips.” said Christophe Fouquet, president & CEO, ASML. “We are pleased by the strong initial support of semiconductor manufacturers, mask suppliers and partners for this initiative.”

“We have always believed that when the industry works together to solve complex problems, we unlock possibilities that no single company could achieve alone,” said TSMC Chairman and CEO Dr. C.C. Wei. “By bringing together expertise from across the industry’s value chain, we hope to keep providing the benefits of cutting-edge technology through continuous innovation that lowers barriers and puts advanced solutions accessible at scale.”

TSMC intends to use ASML’s High NA technology in high-volume manufacturing for advanced nodes starting in 2030. As technology nodes advance, TSMC expects the number of layers requiring High NA EUV will rise, driven primarily by the increasingly complex transistor architectures required for AI applications.

On September 7, in advance of the annual SPIE BACUS Conference in Monterey, California, ASML and TSMC established an industry-wide collaborative initiative to drive the transition to 12-inch photomasks. This effort aims to establish a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031, paving the way for 12-inch High-NA lithography systems to enter advanced node production by 2033.
Underscoring broad industry support, major ecosystem partners and suppliers attended the event and expressed their interest in this transition.

5,000 m² facility expansion combines advanced automation, digital integration and end-to-end product traceability

– Eaton will celebrate the expansion of its manufacturing facility in Schrems, Austria, on 1 October 2026. The expansion supports growing demand driven by electrification and digitalisation across Europe while increasing regional manufacturing capacity for electrical protection and power management solutions. Completed in less than ten months, the expansion combines fully automated production with advanced digital integration and end-to-end product traceability.

"Across Europe, customers are investing in the critical infrastructure that keeps businesses running, supports economic growth and meets rising demand for power. This expansion reflects our continued investment in manufacturing, technology and a skilled workforce, adding capacity for the products and solutions our customers rely on every day,” said Vincent Barro, member of executive leadership team EMEA, Electrical Sector at Eaton.
Supporting European customers through regional manufacturing

Increasing electrification and strong growth in digitalisation are driving demand for robust and efficient power management solutions across the region. Local European manufacturing offers several important benefits for customers including faster response to changing market conditions and customer needs, lower logistics costs and a smaller carbon footprint through proximity to European markets. The facility will provide stability and resilience across critical supply chains while strengthening European manufacturing capabilities and industrial expertise.

Eaton signs agreement to acquire COL Group, expanding manufacturing capacity and capabilities for data center and utility markets in EMEA

– Intelligent power management company Eaton (NYSE:ETN) today announced it has signed an agreement to acquire COL Group from Oaktree’s Power Opportunities strategy. COL Group is a leader in medium-voltage electrical distribution solutions, including SF₆-free switchgear, grid automation technologies and modular power systems. The acquisition will expand Eaton's European power distribution capabilities and manufacturing footprint, enhancing its ability to support growing customer demand across data center and utility markets.

“COL Group brings complementary technologies, manufacturing capabilities and engineering expertise that will further strengthen Eaton's European power distribution platform,” said Omar Zaire, president, EMEA Region, Corporate and Electrical Sector, Eaton. “The acquisition will enhance our ability to support utility and data center customers' increasing need for resilient, sustainable power infrastructure and integrated grid-to-chip power solutions.”
Under the terms of the agreement, Eaton will acquire COL Group for an enterprise value of €810 million. COL Group has forecasted sales of €250 million for 2027.

COL Group is an industrial group with over a century of experience specializing in the development of electrical power distribution solutions. The company has approximately 400 employees and facilities in Turin, Milan, Bergamo, and Catania, Italy.
The transaction, which is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP) is designed to be the first module to support 400Gb/s-per-lane electrical signals, enabling capacity up to 12.8Tb/s so AI factory builders can scale Ethernet AI fabrics, while extending a proven deployment model across multiple generations of data center networks.

USFP delivers 4x the bandwidth density and 1.3x the power efficiency of 200Gb/s-per-lane optics so AI factories can connect more computing systems without adding network tiers, while using less power to move each bit of data.
NVIDIA and Cisco are working with TE Connectivity and Amphenol to build a multi-source hardware ecosystem around USFP.

NVIDIA and Cisco today announced plans for Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a new high-density 400Gb/s-per-lane optical module designed to equip the hardware ecosystem for the next generation of AI factories using pluggable transceivers.

As AI models grow and inference demand expands, AI factories must connect more computing systems while managing network complexity, power and costs. Moving more data per watt and per switch helps operators make better use of their infrastructure investments.

Scaling AI factories requires more bandwidth per connection and more connections per switch. When a switch reaches its capacity, further network expansion can require additional switch layers and optical links, increasing latency, power consumption and costs.

USFP is designed to enable AI factory builders to scale from 200 Gb/s per lane to 400Gb/s-per-lane Ethernet AI fabrics, while extending a deployment model proven at scale across multiple generations of data center networks. With USFP, customers can embrace next-generation optical technology and meet the performance demand of AI workloads without overhauling their data center infrastructure.

The first planned USFP-based transceivers will pack 16 full-duplex lanes in an octal small form factor (OSFP)-sized footprint supporting both switches and SuperNICs, with the ability to expand to 32 and more lanes in the future. By doubling both the lane count and bandwidth per lane, USFP enables AI fabrics to connect more 1.6Tb/s endpoints without adding network tiers. Customers will be able to achieve 12.8Tb/s of overall capacity with USFP.

Comparable with an OSFP-sized module, it delivers 4x the bandwidth and front-panel bandwidth density, with approximately 1.3x the power efficiency, versus 200Gb/s-per-lane pluggable modules. This means AI builders can increase their compute scale within the same network footprint, while decreasing networking’s share of the overall AI factory power budget.

“Building the world’s largest AI factories starts with rethinking the smallest of connections,” said Gilad Shainer, senior vice president NVIDIA. “With USFP, NVIDIA and Cisco are building an ecosystem to reinvent pluggable optics — connecting more computing with greater efficiency to power the next generation of AI factories.”

“AI builders need an interconnect architecture that can scale performance without locking them into a more complex operating model,” said Bill Gartner, senior vice president and general manager of optical systems and optics at Cisco. “Cisco and NVIDIA recognized that scaling pluggable optics to 400Gb/s per lane would require more than another incremental extension of today’s module designs. Through our collaboration, USFP is designed to deliver a new level of bandwidth density while preserving the serviceability, deployment flexibility and operational simplicity of pluggable optics. By taking a full-stack approach — from silicon and systems to optics and the network operating system — we can optimize every layer to deliver the performance and scale the next generation of AI networks will require.”
More AI Infrastructure From Every Switch

Designed for electrical signals of 400Gb/s per lane, USFP uses a new two-dimensional array connector with a two-step insertion design that engages high-speed contacts after the module is inserted, reducing contact wear, improving signal integrity and making insertion force more predictable. The connector technology allows for further scaling of lane count to 32 full duplex lanes and more in the future. Because the connector is designed for 400Gb/s performance, it also offers improved performance at 200Gb/s per lane.

USFP supports power dissipation of up to 100 watts without needing a separate, dedicated embedded cooling circuit within the transceiver, reducing switch design complexity and improving reliability. Together, these capabilities enable higher-bandwidth fabrics while preserving the mature deployment, serviceability and manufacturability of existing pluggable transceivers.

All USFP configurations support optical designs that reduce latency and power consumption by simplifying signal processing. Support for a broad range of optical technologies and connection distances gives system designers the flexibility to meet unique AI factory deployment needs.
A Hardware Ecosystem for Next-Generation AI Factories

NVIDIA and Cisco are collaborating with TE Connectivity and Amphenol to build USFP cages, connectors and modules, with additional partners expected to join. The shared form factor gives suppliers a common foundation for developing high-density pluggable infrastructure for 400Gb/s-per-lane fabrics to build a robust ecosystem for AI factory builders.

NVIDIA announces commitments valued at $1 billion to advance U.S. science over the next five years, at a Washington event convening U.S. officials, industry leaders and members of the science community.
This builds on longstanding collaboration between NVIDIA and national labs, spanning two decades.

NVIDIA today announced commitments valued at $1 billion to build out the United States’ capacity for super intelligence research and development in fields critical for U.S. leadership, including quantum computing, healthcare and energy security.

The announcement was made during the Science: A New Golden Age event in Washington, D.C., where U.S. officials, industry leaders and members of the science community convened on the public-private collaborations needed to bolster scientific exploration.

“President Trump’s Genesis Mission is launching a new golden age of American discovery,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With a $1 billion investment, NVIDIA is putting advanced Super Intelligence in the hands of America’s scientists to accelerate breakthroughs in medicine, energy and materials. This is how America turns scientific leadership into industrial leadership, and innovation into jobs and opportunity for generations.”

During the event, the U.S. Office of Science and Technology Policy celebrated the expansion of the Genesis Mission, of which NVIDIA is a leading industry partner. In response, NVIDIA has invited members of the science community to collaborate in R&D using compute and super intelligence infrastructure resources to accelerate scientific discovery and promote U.S. innovation.
Strengthening US Leadership in Scientific Discovery

Over the next five years, NVIDIA will commit $1 billion to the advancement of super intelligence for science and quantum computing across the U.S. through support of the nation’s higher-education research institutions, investments in accelerating American quantum leadership and support for cloud service providers bolstering U.S. government mission needs.
NVIDIA is also a collaborator on a number of the phase 2 Genesis Mission awards announced today at the event, including projects in quantum computing, fusion, accelerator design and microelectronics.
NVIDIA has collaborated with U.S. national labs for more than two decades. Last year, it announced its partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) on the Genesis Mission, which includes
NVIDIA’s work to build the department’s largest supercomputer for scientific research
at Argonne National Laboratory. This is in addition to supporting
across Argonne and Los Alamos National Laboratories, accelerating the DOE’s mission of driving technological leadership.
NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has authorized a $150 billion increase to the share repurchase program, raising the remaining total program to $235 billion.
This marks the largest share repurchase authorization increase in history.

NVIDIA today announced that its Board of Directors has authorized an additional $150 billion under the company’s existing share repurchase program, increasing the total remaining amount authorized to $235 billion.
The company expects to execute the total remaining program through fiscal year 2028.

“NVIDIA’s growth is being driven by a once-in-a-generation platform shift to AI and accelerated computing,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders. This authorization reflects our confidence in the long-term opportunity ahead.”

Financial Results

thousand units in FY2027 first quarter (the first quarter ended June 30, 2026) compared with FY2026 first quarter
(the first quarter ended June 30, 2025). Vehicle unit sales in Japan increased by 43 thousand units, or 8.9%, to 524
thousand units in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. Meanwhile, overseas vehicle unit
sales decreased by 60 thousand units, or 3.1%, to 1,870 thousand units in FY2027 first quarter compared with
FY2026 first quarter.

TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION FY2027 First Quarter Financial Summary
Segment Operating Results
(1) Automotive:
Sales revenues for the automotive operations increased by 973.1 billion yen, or 8.8%, to 12,012.7
billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. However, operating income decreased
by 191.4 billion yen, or 21.0%, to 719.9 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter.
The decrease in operating income was mainly due to the increase in expenses and others.
(2) Financial services:
Sales revenues for the financial services operations increased by 264.5 billion yen, or 23.3%, to 1,400.6
billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter, and operating income increased by
53.4 billion yen, or 24.0%, to 275.6 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter.
The increase in operating income was mainly due to increase in loan balance.
(3) All other:
Sales revenues for all other businesses increased by 127.0 billion yen, or 37.0%, to 469.9 billion yen
in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter, and operating income increased by 44.2 billion
yen, or 118.0%, to 81.6 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter.
Geographic Information
(1) Japan:
Sales revenues in Japan increased by 613.8 billion yen, or 11.8%, to 5,824.5 billion yen in FY2027
first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. However, operating income decreased by 104.9 billion yen,
or 16.3%, to 540.1 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. The decrease in
operating income was mainly due to the increase in expenses and others.
(2) North America:
Sales revenues in North America increased by 791.5 billion yen, or 14.9%, to 6,105.7 billion yen in
FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter, and operating income increased by 206.6 billion yen
to 185.4 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. The increase in operating
income was mainly due to the decrease in expenses and expense reduction efforts.
(3) Europe:
Sales revenues in Europe increased by 318.2 billion yen, or 20.4%, to 1,879.8 billion yen in FY2027
first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter, and operating income increased by 10.2 billion yen, or 10.6%,
to 107.2 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. The increase in operating
income was mainly due to marketing efforts.
(4) Asia:
Sales revenues in Asia increased by 201.9 billion yen, or 9.5%, to 2,336.3 billion yen in FY2027 first
quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. However, operating income decreased by 7.4 billion yen, or 3.4%,
to 208.3 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. The decrease in operating
income was mainly due to the increase in expenses and others.
(5) Other (Central and South America, Oceania, Africa and the Middle East):
Sales revenues in other regions increased by 144.7 billion yen, or 12.8%, to 1,272.1 billion yen in
FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. However, operating income decreased by 1.5 billion
yen, or 1.6%, to 92.5 billion yen in FY2027 first quarter compared with FY2026 first quarter. The decrease in
operating income was mainly due to the effects of marketing activities.3

2. Consolidated Financial Position for FY2027 First Quarter
Financial Position
The financial position for FY2027 first quarter was as follows:
Total assets decreased by 2,887.2 billion yen, or 2.7%, to 102,635.1 billion yen at the end of FY2027 first
quarter compared with the end of FY2026. Liabilities decreased by 96.0 billion yen, or 0.1%, to 64,406.1 billion
yen at the end of FY2027 first quarter compared with the end of FY2026. Shareholders' equity decreased by
2,791.1 billion yen, or 6.8%, to 38,228.9 billion yen at the end of FY2027 first quarter compared with the end of
FY2026.
Overview of Cash Flow
Cash and cash equivalents decreased by 2,316.5 billion yen, or 18.3%, to 10,343.0 billion yen at the end
of FY2027 first quarter compared with the end of FY2026.
The increases or decreases for each cash flow activity compared with the previous fiscal year are as
follows:
Cash flows from operating activities
Net cash flows from operating activities resulted in an increase in cash by 536.5 billion yen for FY2027
first quarter. Net cash provided by operating activities decreased by 1,339.9 billion yen from 1,876.4 billion yen
for FY2026 first quarter.
Cash flows from investing activities
Net cash flows from investing activities resulted in an increase in cash by 1,427.4 billion yen for FY2027
first quarter. Net cash provided by investing activities increased by 3,229.4 billion yen from 1,802.0 billion yen
net cash used for FY 2026 first quarter.
Cash flows from financing activities
Net cash flows from financing activities resulted in a decrease in cash by 4,339.0 billion yen for FY2027
first quarter. Net cash used in financing activities increased by 3,535.8 billion yen from 803.2 billion yen for
FY2026 first quarter.4

At our earnings announcement in May of this year, we outlined our initiatives for business structure reform. Today, I would like to provide an update on one of these initiatives, specifically our progress in the “enhancement of our earning power.” First, let me discuss the expansion of HEV production capacity. Demand for HEVs remains strong, and the HEV mix continues to rise in many regions around the world. Toyota plans to sell more than 5 million HEVs for the first time in 2026. To steadily meet customer demand, we will continue to expand HEV battery production capacity.

August 5, 2026 For release: Immediately Refer to: Megan MacCauley; maccauley_megan@lilly.com (Media) Mike Czapar; czapar_michael_c@lilly.com (Investors) Lilly reports second-quarter 2026 financial results, raises full-year guidance, and highlights continued growth and pipeline progress • Revenue in Q2 2026 increased 48% to $23.0 billion driven primarily by Mounjaro and Zepbound volume. • Q2 2026 EPS increased by 26% to $7.94 on a reported basis and increased by 33% to $8.38 on a non-GAAP basis.

Q2 2026 reported and non-GAAP EPS included $3.03 of acquired IPR&D charges compared to $0.14 in Q2 2025. • Increased 2026 full-year revenue guidance to be in the range of $85.0 billion to $87.0 billion and raised underlying non-GAAP EPS guidance for the full year by $2.78 at the midpoint, which was more than offset by $3.03 of acquired IPR&D charges from Q2 business development activity, resulting in an updated range of $35.50 to $36.50. • Regulatory progress included U.S.

FDA approval of Ebglyss for one maintenance dose every eight weeks in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, European Commission approval of Jaypirca as monotherapy for adults with chronic lymphocytic leukemia across all lines of therapy, and the submission for orforglipron for type 2 diabetes in the U.S. • Pipeline highlights included positive data from three additional Phase 3 trials of retatrutide in obesity. The clinical data package is now complete to support global registrations for obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and knee osteoarthritis pain, with plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S.

FDA in the first quarter of 2027. • Business development activity in Q2 2026 included the completed acquisitions of Orna Therapeutics, Inc., Ajax Therapeutics, Inc., Centessa Pharmaceuticals plc. and Kelonia Therapeutics, Inc. Subsequent to quarter end, we completed three acquisitions to build an infectious disease portfolio and entered into an agreement to acquire AtaiBeckley, Inc. • Committed an additional $4.5 billion to expand Indiana manufacturing sites. INDIANAPOLIS, August 5, 2026 - Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced its financial results for the second quarter of 2026 and provided updated 2026 financial guidance.

"Lilly's momentum continues, as we delivered 48% revenue growth and raised our full-year guidance," said David A. Ricks, Lilly chair and CEO. "At the same time, Lilly is building for the future. With our next- generation weight-loss medicine retatrutide and its complete clinical data package in hand, new manufacturing capacity coming online, and exciting new assets entering our pipeline through business development, Lilly's future, after 150 years, has never been brighter." grew to $15.7 billion in Q2 2026, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound. Key Products revenue in the
Immunology, Oncology, and Neuroscience therapeutic areas grew 121% in Q2 2026 compared to Q2
2025.
Revenue in the U.S. increased 33% to $14.4 billion, driven by a 37% increase in volume, partially offset
by a 3% decrease in realized prices. The increase in U.S. volume was driven by Zepbound and Mounjaro.

adjustments to estimates for rebates and discounts primarily driven by Trulicity, Zepbound, and Mounjaro.

primarily by the addition of Mounjaro to the National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL) in China. The

Lilly reports first-quarter 2026 financial results, raises full year guidance, and highlights
momentum of new medicines
• Revenue in Q1 2026 increased 56% to $19.8 billion primarily driven by volume growth, partially
offset by lower realized prices from Mounjaro and Zepbound.
• Q1 2026 EPS increased by 170% to $8.26 on a reported basis and increased by 156% to $8.55
on a non-GAAP basis. The Q1 2026 reported and non-GAAP EPS included $0.52 of acquired
IPR&D charges compared to $1.72 in Q1 2025.
• Increased 2026 full-year revenue guidance to be in the range of $82.0 billion to $85.0 billion and
non-GAAP EPS guidance to be in the range of $35.50 to $37.00.
• Regulatory progress included U.S. FDA approval of Foundayo (orforglipron) for adults with
obesity, or overweight with weight-related medical problems.
• Pipeline progress included positive Phase 3 results from Foundayo (orforglipron) in adults with
type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight at increased cardiovascular risk, Jaypirca in
combination with venetoclax and rituximab in relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL, Taltz and
Zepbound used together for adults with psoriasis and obesity or overweight, and retatrutide in
type 2 diabetes.
• Business development activity included the agreements to acquire Orna Therapeutics, Centessa
Pharmaceuticals plc., Kelonia Therapeutics, and Ajax Therapeutics.
• Company announces planned Investment Community Meeting for December 7, 2026
INDIANAPOLIS, April 30, 2026 - Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced its financial results
for the first quarter of 2026 and provided updated 2026 financial guidance.
"2026 is off to a strong start, we delivered 56% revenue growth in the first quarter and raised our full-year
revenue guidance by $2 billion," said David A. Ricks, Lilly chair and CEO. “A key milestone was the U.S.
FDA approval of Foundayo—the only approved GLP-1 pill that can be taken any time of day, without food
and water restrictions. Foundayo will meaningfully expand the number of people who can benefit from
GLP-1s. We also delivered pipeline progress across all four therapeutic areas and continued investing in
Lilly's future growth through four acquisitions.”

First-Quarter Reported Results
In Q1 2026, worldwide revenue was $19.8 billion, an increase of 56% compared with Q1 2025, driven by
a 65% increase in volume, partially offset by a 13% decrease due to lower realized prices. Key Products1
revenue grew to $13.4 billion in Q1 2026, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound. Key Products revenue in the
Immunology, Oncology, and Neuroscience therapeutic areas grew 160% in Q1 2026 compared to Q1
2025.
Revenue in the U.S. increased 43% to $12.1 billion, driven by a 49% increase in volume, partially offset
by a 7% decrease due to lower realized prices. The increase in U.S. volume was driven by Zepbound and
Mounjaro and the decline in realized prices was primarily driven by Zepbound and Taltz.
Revenue outside the U.S. increased 81% to $7.7 billion, driven by a 95% increase in volume, partially
offset by a 25% decrease due to lower realized prices. The lower realized prices outside the U.S. were
driven primarily by the addition of Mounjaro to the National Reimbursed Drug List (NRDL) in China. The
volume increase outside the U.S. was driven by Mounjaro. Jardiance revenue outside the U.S. included
one-time benefits of $250 million in Q1 2026 compared to $370 million in Q1 2025, associated with the
company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim.

Gross margin increased 54% to $16.2 billion in Q1 2026. Gross margin as a percent of revenue was
81.9%, a decrease of 0.6 percentage points versus the same quarter last year. The change was primarily
driven by lower realized prices.
In Q1 2026, research and development expenses increased 28% to $3.5 billion, or 18% of revenue,
driven by continued investments in the company's early and late-stage portfolio.
Marketing, selling, and administrative expenses increased 19% to $2.9 billion in Q1 2026, primarily driven
by promotional efforts supporting ongoing and planned launches.
In Q1 2026, the company recognized acquired in-process research and development (IPR&D) charges of
$584 million compared with $1.6 billion in Q1 2025. The Q1 2025 charges primarily related to the
acquisition of Scorpion Therapeutics, Inc.'s PI3Kα inhibitor program STX-478.
Asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges of $279 million in Q1 2026 were primarily
related to litigation matters. In Q1 2025, there was a charge of $35 million related to intangible asset
impairments.
The effective tax rate was 16.4% in Q1 2026 compared with 20.2% in Q1 2025, primarily driven by the
unfavorable tax impact of a non-deductible acquired IPR&D charge in Q1 2025. The 2026 and 2025
effective tax rates were impacted by net discrete tax benefits in each period.
In Q1 2026, net income and earnings per share (EPS) were $7.4 billion and $8.26, respectively,
compared with net income of $2.8 billion and EPS of $3.06 in Q1 2025. EPS in Q1 2026 and Q1 2025
included acquired IPR&D charges of $0.52 and $1.72, respectively.

The non-GAAP effective tax rate was 16.5% in Q1 2026 compared with 20.2% in Q1 2025, primarily
driven by the unfavorable tax impact of a non-deductible acquired IPR&D charge in Q1 2025. The 2026
and 2025 effective tax rates were impacted by net discrete tax benefits in each period.

INDIANAPOLIS, February 4, 2026 - Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced its financial
results for the fourth-quarter of 2025 and provided 2026 financial guidance.
"2025 was an important year for Lilly," said David A. Ricks, Lilly's chair and CEO. "We reached millions
more patients—launching Inluriyo, expanding Mounjaro and Kisunla globally, and submitting orforglipron
for approval. We expanded our manufacturing capacity, and through our U.S. government agreement,
opened new access to obesity medicines. Entering our 150th year with a deep pipeline and platforms like
LillyDirect, we're positioned to reach more patients than ever and expand our global health impact."

Fourth-Quarter Reported Results
In Q4 2025, worldwide revenue was $19.3 billion, an increase of 43% compared with Q4 2024, driven by
a 46% increase in volume, partially offset by a 5% decrease due to lower realized prices. Key Products1
revenue grew to $13.8 billion in Q4 2025, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound.
Revenue in the U.S. increased 43% to $12.9 billion, driven by a 50% increase in volume, partially offset
by a 7% decrease due to lower realized prices. The increase in U.S. volume and decline in realized prices
were driven by Zepbound and Mounjaro.
Revenue outside the U.S. increased 43% to $6.4 billion, driven by a 38% increase in volume and to a
lesser extent a 4% favorable impact on foreign exchange rates. The volume increase outside the U.S.
was driven primarily by Mounjaro, partially offset by Jardiance. Volume growth was negatively impacted
by a one-time benefit of $300 million related to Jardiance, associated with an amendment to the
company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim, in Q4 2024.

82.5%, an increase of 0.3 percentage points. The increase in gross margin percent was primarily driven
by favorable product mix and improved cost of production, partially offset by lower realized prices.

AMD Helion lets customers tailor CPU core density, performance and power to agentic workloads, with CPU-only configurations for hyperscale deployments and integrated CPU/GPU configurations for enterprises.
AMD Helion combines open hardware and software with an integrated token router that directs agents’ model calls across frontier and open-source models.
(NASDAQ: AMD) today introduced the AMD Helion agentic AI rack, an open blueprint for agentic AI infrastructure based on an Open Compute Project spec-design and powered by AMD compute.

Building on the open-platform approach of the AMD Helios™ rackscale solution, AMD Helion is designed to provide partners and customers with the flexibility they need for agentic AI infrastructure. With AMD Helion, customers can match CPU performance, core density and power with GPU acceleration for the work their AI agents perform.

“Agentic AI is not a single workload. It spans personal agents, enterprise applications, code execution and complex workflows, each with different compute requirements,” said Dan McNamara, senior vice president and general manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD. “To do that takes optimized compute and infrastructure that can adapt to different workloads. With AMD Helion, we are bringing AMD EPYC™ performance, open software and flexible rack designs together so our partners can build systems around customer needs and make efficient use of available power.”

AMD Helion’s OCP spec-based rack blueprint supports open software and can come in flexible configurations, including liquid- and air-cooled versions, allowing customers to create virtually any configuration needed for their needs. Some examples of this include:

A CPU-only rack powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors that can support up to 32,768 CPU cores. This rack is designed for hyperscale customers, providing dedicated capacity for agent execution and connections to separate model inference infrastructure.

An all-in-one rack that combines AMD EPYC CPU nodes, AMD Instinct™ MI350P GPU nodes and general-purpose compute on one platform. This rack is designed to provide partners and customers an all-in-one concept for enterprise agentic AI.

AMD Helion enables customers to deploy agentic AI in the IT infrastructure they already have, turning existing investments into a foundation for new AI capabilities. Partners can tailor CPU and GPU configurations to customer workloads, matching agent execution, model inference and supporting compute to each deployment’s performance, power and cost requirements.

AMD plans to contribute the AMD Helion specification to OCP, making it available to the community for further development and adoption. AMD Helion agentic rack configurations are currently under development with ecosystem partners and are planned to be available in November 2026.

AMD is helping shape the next phase of AI infrastructure through open, flexible platforms, a broad portfolio of workload-optimized compute and collaboration across the ecosystem. AMD Helion brings that approach to agentic AI, helping partners match software and compute to the work agents perform and giving customers flexibility to scale as their requirements evolve.

Agentic AI is changing what customers need from their infrastructure. It's not just about compute performance, but how the entire system is connected, managed and secured. Architectures like AMD Helion, combined with Cisco's full-stack infrastructure capabilities, can give customers greater flexibility to deploy, operate and scale agentic workloads into their environments as their needs evolve.

The Group will continue to leverage its strengths in rack-level system integration and global manufacturing, working with ecosystem partners to advance rack-scale Agentic AI solutions and accelerate next-generation AI infrastructure deployment.

Announcing Intel® Inference Microservices: Tuned LLM Inference on Intel® Processors
Intel® Inference Microservices make it easy to get tuned LLM performance on existing Intel® processors, eliminating days of complex, manual hardware optimization.

Getting a large language model to respond is easy. Getting it to respond well, repeatedly, on the hardware you already own is the part that can take a week. Precision, how work is distributed across cores, how memory is laid out across NUMA nodes, and which instruction sets the engine uses all depend on both the model and the processor beneath it. Change the model and the good settings change. Move to a different generation of silicon and they change again.

. Each microservice is a container that serves one model behind an OpenAI compatible API and configures itself for the Intel® processor it detects at startup, using settings Intel® tuned and validated for that model on that silicon. You pick the model. The container picks the settings.

This first release runs on Intel® Xeon® processors, and it is the first step toward a single inference interface across Intel® hardware. A microservice serves one model on one host. When you need a fleet of them, shared across teams with security and routing already handled, the

That is the only command. On startup the container inspects the processor it landed on, selects the best available configuration profile for that model on that hardware, and applies it for you. There is nothing for you to tune and nothing to work out first.

That is the whole integration. No custom protocol, no Intel® SDK, no Python environment to build, and no engine to install.
Most AI frameworks already speak the OpenAI API, so pointing one at that base URL is all it takes: the OpenAI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, and Haystack all work unchanged, streaming included.
What It Changes for the Business

Faster time to production, at the tuned configuration. Tuning, benchmarking, and adjusting for each model on each platform is replaced by a pull and a run, and what you pull is the configuration that performed best in Intel® Hardware.

No new hardware to procure. Inference becomes a scheduling decision against Intel® Xeon® capacity you already own, not a capital purchase, so a project can start this quarter rather than after a procurement cycle.

A wider pool of developers can ship AI. Application developers change a base URL. Deploying a model no longer needs an inference optimization specialist, which is the bottleneck most enterprise AI programs actually hit.
One pattern to standardize on. A validated profile plus a pinned tag means the same model behaves the same way on every matching host, under Docker and under Kubernetes alike.

What you build now carries forward. The interface is the contract, not the silicon. This release runs on Intel® Xeon®, and as Intel® Inference Microservices extend across the rest of the Intel® hardware portfolio the API in front of them stays the same, so moving a workload onto different Intel® hardware later is a deployment change rather than an application rewrite.
Your data stays put. Models run in your environment, on your hardware.
An OpenAI compatible API on a port of your choosing, 8000 by default: chat completions, completions, models, health, and Prometheus metrics
What Intel® Inference Microservices sets for you
Precision, core and work distribution, and memory layout, for your model on this processor
4th, 5th, or 6th Gen Intel® Xeon® processors, 32 GB RAM suggested. Intel® GPU support planned
OpenAI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, Haystack. Change the base URL only

Performance is the reason the profile exists. Precision, how work is spread across cores, and how memory is laid out are what decide how much a host delivers, and finding the right combination is normally a week of benchmarking for every model on every platform. Each container ships with the best configuration Intel® measured for that model on that processor, so the tuned path is the one that runs by default.
Figure 1. Your application talks to an OpenAI compatible API. The microservice container sits between that API and the Intel® processor underneath it.

At startup the container inspects the host it landed on processor generation, how many cores it was given, how many NUMA nodes the machine has, and which built in accelerators the processor offers. That last one is where the real acceleration comes from. Recent Intel® Xeon® cores carry dedicated engines for exactly the math inference spends its time on, Intel® Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel® AMX) for the matrix multiplication at the heart of a model and the vector extensions (AVX-512, AVX2, and VNNI) for the work around it. They are already in the silicon you own, and they only pay off if the serving engine knows they are there and is configured to use them.

Those findings select a validated profile, the runtime resolves the tuned engine parameters, weights are cached, and the optimized inference engine starts behind the API on the port you mapped, 8000 by default. In this release that engine is vLLM. Two hosts with similar product names can legitimately get different settings if their capabilities differ, which is the point. Constrain the container and it configures for the constraint, not for the host.

What happens when nothing matches depends on which container you run. The model specific images ship with the general profile fallback disabled, so an unrecognized host surfaces as an error at startup rather than as a quietly untuned deployment you discover later in a benchmark. That is the conservative default on purpose: the only configurations those images will run are ones Intel® measured for that model. The base image, the one you point at any model on Hugging Face, defaults the other way with profile fallback `enabled`. When no model specific profile matches, selection uses a compatible general profile instead, one that is model agnostic and tuned to the hardware rather than to the model.
You can see what it found without serving anything, and dry-run will print the resolved profile and the exact vLLM command it would execute:

docker run --rm intel/inference-xeon-base:0.1.0 detect-hardware
docker run --rm intel/inference-xeon-qwen-qwen3-4b:0.1.0 dry-run --format json

“The optimizations behind this release are the same ones Intel® contributes in the open, upstream in the frameworks enterprises already build on, including vLLM. Intel® Inference Microservices package that work behind a standard API, so customers get a tuned stack without doing the tuning themselves. We are committed to continue contributing optimizations upstream as we extend the same interface across our hardware portfolio."
-Bill Pearson, Intel vice president, Data Center Software, Data Center Group
A First Step Toward Unified Inference on Intel®

This first release targets Intel® Xeon® processors with vLLM at BF16 across 4th, 5th, and 6th Gen, on Docker or Kubernetes 1.24+. Tool calling and structured output are reachable today as vLLM pass throughs rather than validated capabilities. A Helm chart, a Kubernetes Operator, additional inference engines, and additional precisions are planned for later releases.
Each model carries its own license, shown on the model's listing in the
. Users are responsible for complying with the license terms of the model they deploy.

Intel® Xeon® is where this starts, not where it stops. The contract a microservice presents is deliberately independent of the silicon behind it: one container per model, an OpenAI compatible API on a known port, and a runtime that detects the platform it lands on and applies the profile Intel® validated for that combination. Nothing in that contract is specific to a CPU. As the portfolio broadens to Intel® GPUs, including the data center inference GPU codenamed Crescent Island , the same microservice model extends to them. The profile that gets selected changes. The interface your application talks to does not.

That is the point of unifying on one interface. Build against Intel® Xeon® today, on processors already in the fleet and available at ubiquitous scale, then move the same workload to an Intel® GPU when model size or economics call for it, without rewriting the application, tuning it again for the new platform, or standing up a second serving stack beside the first. The choice of silicon becomes a deployment decision rather than an engineering project, and it stays a reversible one. A single API spanning general-purpose CPUs and dedicated inference GPUs provides a consistent portability path across Intel® platforms.

That the interface can stay this stable is not a packaging trick. It holds because the work underneath it goes upstream: native integration with the standard frameworks and open inference engines teams already run, with Intel®'s optimizations contributed to those projects rather than locked inside a vendor-specific toolkit. A tuned container stays a standard OpenAI compatible endpoint instead of becoming an SDK you have to adopt. On the front lines of crisis management, where timely decisions are critical, control rooms are evolving to meet the demands of today’s highly connected society. Moving beyond traditional monitoring, they have become centralized hubs that manage growing volumes of video and data while overseeing communications networks.

From industrial operations to sports and critical infrastructure, organizations around the world are turning to Samsung’s The Wall. Among them are the Iskandar Puteri Command and Control Centre (IPCCC), the integrated operations center for Iskandar Puteri City Council, Johor, Malaysia; and NASCAR, one of the world’s leading motorsports organizations.
▲ The Wall at the Iskandar Puteri Command and Control Centre’s control room
While the information displayed on screen varies across industries, every control room requires robust security and unwavering reliability.

The Wall uses the industry-standard Advanced Encryption Standard 128-bit (AES-128) encryption algorithm and Samsung’s proprietary Knox Security platform to securely encrypt data transmitted from S-Box to Cabinet.

AES-128, a symmetric-key encryption algorithm adopted by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), protects sensitive control room information while enabling fast data transmission and reception.

Designed for uninterrupted 24/7 operation, The Wall incorporates redundant power and signal systems. If an unexpected power failure or signal error occurs, the backup system activates immediately to ensure continuous monitoring and control.
The Wall’s modular chip-on-board (COB) architecture allows individual modules to be replaced quickly while the display remains on, minimizing downtime. With an LED lifespan
of up to 150,000 hours — among the longest in the industry – it also helps reduce long-term total cost of ownership (TCO).

Optimized for control room environments, The Wall offers a modular, scalable design that can be customized to virtually any space. Advanced display technology ensures large volumes of information are presented with clarity and precision.
: Cross-Agency Coordination for Faster Emergency Response

Urban crises often unfold as a chain of interconnected events. For example, if a water main bursts, traffic may need to be redirected immediately. If a major traffic accident occurs, firefighters conducting rescue operations and police managing the scene must coordinate in real time.

In Johor, Malaysia, IPCCC uses Samsung’s The Wall to support integrated city monitoring and coordination among relevant agencies. IPCCC selected The Wall for its image quality, color richness, and brightness, as well as Samsung’s reputation as a reliable long-term technology partner.
▲ The Wall supports IPCCC’s city operations monitoring with an immersive visual experience.

IPCCC brings together traffic, public safety, and environmental monitoring data onto a single, unified display. Anchoring the operations center is Malaysia’s longest The Wall installation, spanning 19.35 meters and capturing the city’s vast network of information on one screen.

Today, the massive display serves as the command hub for citywide operations — from security monitoring to coordinated incident response. By consolidating this information, The Wall supports stronger inter-agency coordination across departments.
▲ The Wall helps IPCCC city operations teams monitor traffic, public safety, and city services.

“Installing a curved large-scale display allows us to maximize the space while maintaining an efficient operational layout for our workstation and war room,” said Farah Izzati Binti Muhamad Fuad, Director of the Smart City Unit at IPCCC. “The ultra-wide screen enables us to monitor multiple smart safety systems, improving coordination and allowing our team to respond more quickly to incidents.”

Beyond public services, control systems also play a critical role in sports — where capturing every moment of the action is essential. In motorsports, where speeds exceed 290 kilometers per hour and up to 40 cars race in close formation, officials must assess incidents and make decisions in fractions of a second.
▲ The Wall provides NASCAR’s Remote Race Control center with a large, clear view of live race data, video feeds, and on-track conditions.

NASCAR, the most popular motorsport in the U.S., built its Remote Race Control center around The Wall to support race control staff at the track with additional monitoring, analysis, and replay capabilities. Measuring 9.75 meters wide and 2.74 meters high, the massive display provides up to 24 officials a shared, high-resolution view, giving them the visual clarity to review and manage split-second race incidents together.

Equipped with a Micro AI Processor, The Wall analyzes complex live footage in real time to reduce noise. This enables dynamic camera feeds from around the track to be displayed in ultra-high definition with minimal noise and motion blur, helping officials make fast, accurate decisions.

At the launch in 2025, Steve Stum, NASCAR Vice President of Operations and Technical Production, highlighted the visibility that Remote Race Control would provide through more than 200 camera angles and multiple data points from every car, along with its potential to enable faster, more accurate competition calls and improve the racing product. Now in its second season of operation, the remote race control room gives officials greater visibility across races and supports more efficient and accurate officiating.
By consolidating multiple video feeds and data streams on The Wall, the remote race control room enables officials to view more information simultaneously and share feeds for collaborative review.
Describing the experience, Scott Miller, competition strategist at NASCAR, said, “It’s like having 20 monitors in front of you, as opposed to probably two or three sitting at a single work station.”
▲ Samsung technology supports NASCAR’s Remote Race Control center at its production facility in Concord, North Carolina.

Control rooms across industries are evolving to meet increasingly complex demands — whether ensuring the stable operation of infrastructure, enabling integrated citywide monitoring, or supporting live sports where decisions made in fractions of a second can make all the difference. Regardless of the application, every control room depends on a display that helps operators process vast amounts of information and make fast, accurate decisions. As a safe and reliable visual hub for mission-critical operations, Samsung’s The Wall will continue to provide the clarity needed to support decision-making across major industries worldwide.

Samsung Electronics today announced that it is bringing together global telecommunications industry partners at the Samsung Research America campus in Mountain View, California for the Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 on Oct. 15 (local time), following Partner Day held at the same venue the prior day.

Telecommunications experts from major global operators, manufacturers, government agencies, and academia are participating in the events, with more than 100 attendees gathering to exchange insights and explore the future of next-generation networks.
▲ A view of Partner Day in Mountain View, California, on Oct 14

Samsung is discussing the evolution of software-driven networks for the AI and 6G eras, as well as ecosystem-wide collaboration that creates new value across the telecommunications industry. The company is also showcasing its leadership in 6G communication technology, sharing achievements in AI-native technologies applied to its communication systems, and providing other updates.
Collaboration To Create New Network Value in the AI Era

Partner Day fostered engaging conversations grounded in the expertise and experience of leaders from across the industry. Participants examined software-driven network strategies and ecosystem-wide collaboration as the convergence of AI and networks accelerates the evolution of network infrastructure.

Samsung opened the event with a keynote highlighting the way AI is transforming the architectural foundation that has defined telecommunications networks for more than a century. The company emphasized that, moving beyond the limitations of existing technologies, the convergence of connectivity and AI will be a key driver of new ways of communication that humanity has long imagined. Drawing on the industry’s collective intelligence, Samsung then delved into the strategic direction of network evolution in the AI era.
▲ Woojune Kim, President and Head of Networks Business at Samsung Electronics, is giving his keynote speech at Partner Day, on Oct 14.

The panel sessions centered on experiences and key lessons learned from the commercialization of virtualized networks, exploring how the ecosystem can continue to evolve. Participants also discussed ways to move beyond connectivity by developing new services and translating them into tangible business opportunities.

“Networks in the AI era are evolving into intelligent infrastructure that can understand the diverse requirements of a growing range of new services, flexibly adapt through virtualization, and deliver optimal solutions for each need,” said Angelo Jeongho Park, Executive Vice President and Head of Global Strategic Sales, Networks Business at Samsung Electronics. “Together with our industry-leading partners, Samsung has successfully commercialized virtualized networks at scale. By adding advanced AI technologies to that foundation, we will transform communications infrastructure into a new engine for growth and lead the way toward the industry’s next leap forward.”

The Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit is opening with keynote presentations from telecommunications industry experts, followed by three panel sessions — “AI-Native 6G Networks,” “Taking 6G to Space With NTN,” and “Connecting the Physical and Digital Worlds” — along with technology demonstrations. Each session includes a lecture on the topic, as well as panel discussions that facilitate dynamic exchanges between participants.

The “AI-Native 6G Networks” session positions AI as the core technology driving innovation in network performance and operational efficiency, with discussion centered on the technical challenges and global collaboration needed to evolve 6G into a truly intelligent network infrastructure.

The “Taking 6G to Space With NTN” session reviews the current status and outlook of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, discusses the technical barriers of space-based communication and satellite connectivity as a potential solution, and addresses satellite communication standards and roadmaps currently under discussion within the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP).

Concluding the day is the “Connecting the Physical and Digital Worlds” session, where participants are discussing new ways to deliver next-generation user experiences by sensing physical spaces and seamlessly linking them to digital services, such as Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) and physical AI.

The technology demonstration session showcases cutting-edge 6G core technologies jointly developed and validated by Samsung and partner companies, including AI RAN implementations, eXtreme Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (X-MIMO) systems, Distributed MIMO (D-MIMO) technologies, and ISAC. Samsung is demonstrating field validation results for the performance of AI-enabled RAN across all layers, transmission performance in the 6G candidate frequency band (7 GHz band), the user experience at cell boundaries, and sensing performance that utilizes base station infrastructure.
▲ An overview of the 6G core technology exhibition booth operated by Samsung Research at the event venue in Mountain View, Silicon Valley, on Oct. 14-15

“Together, 6G and AI-native technologies represent the next step in telecommunications, bringing people closer together than ever before,” said Jinguk Jeong, Executive Vice President and Head of the Advanced Communications Research Center at Samsung Research. “The Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 demonstrates our commitment to closely collaborating with industry partners to advance telecommunications.”

Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 and Partner Day come amid Samsung’s efforts to expand its collaboration on 6G and AI-native communication technology with global partners, including telecommunications operators, research institutes, and business groups.

This year, Samsung has initiated collaboration with LG U+ and conducted field validation with Verizon at a major international soccer fan event in Dallas, Texas, for ISAC technology development. The company is also strengthening research partnerships with major telecommunications operators globally, including NTT DOCOMO, KDDI Research, KT, SK Telecom, and SoftBank. These collaborations are part of ongoing efforts to make 6G technology a reality.

Samsung will continue to deepen collaboration with global partners and advance research at the convergence of AI and communications. By connecting its research strengths with business expertise, the company aims to translate innovation into greater value for the industry and reinforce its leadership in AI-native, 6G networks.

VELDHOVEN, the Netherlands, October 14, 2026 – Today, ASML Holding NV (ASML) has published its 2026 third-quarter results.
Q3 total net sales of €11.7 billion, gross margin of 57.5%, net income of €5.0 billion
ASML expects Q4 2026 total net sales between €14.2 billion and €15.2 billion, and a gross margin around 57%
Full-year 2026 total net sales expected to be between €44 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin around 56%

"In the third quarter we reported a record total net sales of €11.7 billion, towards the high end of our guidance, reflecting the strong execution of our ramp-up. Installed Base Management sales
came in above guidance at €3.3 billion as a result of the continued strong demand for productivity upgrades. This drove the gross margin above guidance at 57.5%.

"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030.

"With such strong visibility and an order book momentum that continues to increase quarter on quarter this year, we now expect that our supply as currently planned for both 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of our customers

. Given this, we are investigating ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase we previously communicated. In addition, we continue to provide significant wafer capacity to our customers through our productivity upgrade portfolio.

"We expect fourth-quarter 2026 total net sales between €14.2 billion and €15.2 billion, with a gross margin around 57%. We expect R&D costs of around €1.2 billion and SG&A costs of around €0.4 billion. We expect total net sales for 2026 to be between €44 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin around 56%," said ASML President and Chief Executive Officer Christophe Fouquet.
Update share buyback program and dividend
In the third quarter, we purchased around €4.1 billion worth of shares under the current 2026–2028 share buyback program.
An interim dividend over 2026 of €1.88 per ordinary share will be made payable on November 4, 2026.

ASML begins construction of new Eindhoven campus, strengthening its presence in the Brainport region
Groundbreaking ceremony was held Tuesday September 8, 2026 at Brainport Industries Campus North
New campus will add manufacturing capacity in support of ASML’s planned growth needs

VELDHOVEN, the Netherlands, September 8, 2026 – ASML Holding N.V. (ASML) today marked the start of construction of its second major industrial campus in the Brainport region, the Netherlands. Together with partners, the company celebrated the milestone with a groundbreaking ceremony at Brainport Industries Campus (BIC) North, launching a multi-phase development project that will eventually span approximately 350,000 square meters and provide potential capacity for up to 20,000 workplaces.

The new location ensures that key activities remain closely connected within the region and are an integral part of the company’s global network. The milestone was celebrated during a ceremony attended by the Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and representatives from government, customers, suppliers, knowledge institutions and regional partners.

"The growing global demand from the semiconductor industry requires continuous investments," said Christophe Fouquet, President and CEO of ASML. "As part of our global expansion plans, BIC North provides the space and flexibility we need to continue innovating and supporting our customers around the world. It will complement our existing office space and manufacturing capacity in the Brainport region and further strengthen our footprint in the Netherlands. This milestone would not have been possible without close collaboration with local, regional and national authorities and we are particularly grateful for the support we have received from the City of Eindhoven."
A new location, introducing an innovative way of working

The first phase of BIC North, expected to be completed in 2029, will house at least 3,000 employees, bringing together production, logistics and supporting office activities in one integrated industrial campus. These workplaces are primarily intended for teams relocating from existing ASML locations.

A key element of the campus will be ASML’s new flow factory, ASML’s next-generation innovative manufacturing operating model for the TWINSCAN factory. This model is designed to enable faster, more efficient and higher-scale module production and installation. It streamlines the flow of materials and work through the factory, helping improve productivity while maintaining high-quality standards. The approach follows proven models used in other industries such as automotive and aerospace.
Future footprint in the Brainport region
In the long term, the BIC campus could accommodate up to 20,000 workplaces, depending on future requirements, providing the flexibility needed to support industry growth.

ASML’s future footprint in the Brainport region will comprise three complementary campuses: a dedicated headquarters campus (De Run 1000) and an industrial campus (De Run 6000/7000) in Veldhoven, alongside the company’s second industrial campus at BIC North in Eindhoven. Together, these locations will support ASML’s innovation, manufacturing and corporate activities in the region.

The development of BIC North reflects the close collaboration between ASML, governments, knowledge institutions and many other stakeholders. Through public-private partnerships, ASML and its partners continue to invest in long-term priorities such as talent development, affordable housing and equal opportunity, helping to support sustainable growth for both the company and the Brainport region.

using the industry's current mask format, either by floor-planning within the 6-inch mask or by utilizing Intel Foundry’s stitching capabilities and process design kit (PDK) solutions.

, working closely with ASML, mask makers, automation suppliers, EDA partners, materials providers, and semiconductor manufacturers to advance the standards, infrastructure, and technology needed to support future High NA scaling.

, the 11th Hyundai Commission, presents a major new multisensory installation by artist and composer Tarek Atoui
